Explore an aggregated tsibble through its series and dimension graphs

Source: R/graph_explore.R
graph_explore.Rd

Serves a browser app for exploring an aggregated tsibble. The left column holds the series graph, drawn on demand, above the dimension graph of the key combinations given to fabletools::aggregate_key(). The right column plots the focused series, with forecasts when a fable is given, above a view of its children or of the pinned series.

Usage

graph_explore(
  data,
  value = NULL,
  forecasts = NULL,
  level = c(80, 95),
  max_points = 1000,
  port = httpuv::randomPort(),
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  launch = interactive(),
  block = !interactive()
)

Arguments

data

An aggregated tsibble, as produced by fabletools::aggregate_key().

value

The measured variable shown first. Every numeric measured variable can be chosen in the app. Defaults to the first.

forecasts

A fable of forecasts for data, with the same keys (and optionally .model). Its response variable must be a measured variable of data. Each model's mean and intervals are drawn after the data.

level

Interval levels drawn for forecasts.

max_points

Series more than twice this long are sent as the minimum and maximum of blocks of time, about max_points values, so spikes stay visible. The season and stacked plots always get the full series.

port, host

Where the app is served.

launch

Open the app in a browser.

block

Block the R session while serving. When FALSE, stop the app with plumber2::api_stop() on the returned api.

Value

The plumber2 api, invisibly.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  library(fable)
  tourism_agg <- aggregate_key(
    tsibble::tourism, Purpose * (State / Region), Trips = sum(Trips)
  )

  # The structure is inferred from the keys: Purpose * (State / Region)
  app <- graph_explore(tourism_agg)
  plumber2::api_stop(app)

  # With forecasts, drawn after the data with their intervals
  tourism_fit <- model(tourism_agg, ets = ETS(Trips), snaive = SNAIVE(Trips))
  tourism_fc <- forecast(tourism_fit, h = "2 years")
  app <- graph_explore(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc)
  plumber2::api_stop(app)
}
